title: Dirichlet nonvanishing at 0.87341198: a selected-norm leaf for the native step, without the density chain
description: Proves all-moduli Dirichlet nonvanishing for Re(s) > 43670599/50000000 = 0.87341198, with the principal pole excluded. (1) Selected root energy (R1, `R1/`, theorem `selectedRootEnergy`). For every cut K in [0.500001, 3/4]: on the natural rows whose prime-slot block D carries mass at least Z^{K w(D)}, the energy of the packed polynomial is at most Z^{M + selExcess + eps}, where selExcess = (P + s + (M - P)_+/5 - M)_+, P is the plain length, s the slot weight and M the row width. The energy of these rows splits exactly over sixth-root classes z = u g^6. Each class is bounded in two ways: directly, by the selected all-source sextic norm of joint-detector-fine-chain (Joseph Bebel, PR 93); and reflectively, by the baseline's reflected radial engine applied to the radical row character of the class, whose conductor is at most N(u)N(g) = Z^M N(g)^{-5}. The classes are summed with the root zeta value and min(a, b) <= a^{1-t} b^t. (2) Selected leaf. In Sil's cube-free native step (sil-density-split-20261026), the heavy rows of the leaf are priced by max(K * deletion need, selExcess) at K = 501/1000. The native gates hold with Sil's cut 3/4 replaced by K, which moves the overshoot gate from 6KB/(1+K) = 2.5714B to about 2.0027B. (3) Lines of faces by continuous induction. The faces are proven on whole lines rather than by a step chain. One induction (`curve_induction`) gives the native line c(Lambda) = 3/50 + (80/2297)(93/25 - Lambda), from the fourth-power source G(99999/100000, 93/25, 3/50) of arvi-repeated-marks-on-sil-face-20261025 down to Lambda = 5143/2000 (steps of at most 1/100000). A second gives the selected-leaf line c(Lambda) = 1/10 + (3/50)(5143/2000 - Lambda), from there down to Lambda = 401/200 (steps of at most 1/200000, selection a = 1/1000). The gates are proven for every step of each line; no step data is stored. The end face is G(99999/100000, 401/200, 13399/100000). No density chain is used: arvi-density's 129-step marked chain, Sil's density step, density-split-fine-chain's ChainK15 and Collet's density lemmas leave the import closure (4484 submission modules instead of 4918 for arvi-density, and 26% fewer olean bytes). (4) Return. arvi-density's return is retuned so that the end face serves both the count and the physical queries. The natural join and the plain floor are freed (s_minus = 27/1000, m_minus = 3/10); physical cap 3/25, numerator cap 3/40, h = 8001361/10000000; three windows, certified reflectively (`Tuning/`). `JointDetector/` holds the 114 modules of joint-detector-fine-chain that the selected norm needs, unchanged except for their import paths. `Return/` holds the 14 modules of arvi-density's return that read its constants, unchanged except for the imports and the retuned constants; the rest of that return is imported from arvi-density. Builds on OpenAI, Hailey Collet, Sil, Jacob Sussman, Joseph Bebel and our earlier work; inherited notices and licenses are retained. The research and Lean development were AI-assisted.
